verifier_notes: Every url was re-opened on 2026-10-02 with the kit's own User-Agent and the text around each name read. All 22 findings were confirmed on the page cited.

Corrected wording: the four website entries said the site was also the one filed with the Secretary of State. The verifier could not see that for itself (the Secretary's sites are not requested, and no saved copy of the filed addresses was found), so the sentence was taken out. Each site still names the candidate and the office or place, which is what the rule asks.
None of the three campaign home pages for Kistler, Parkin or Puschinsky prints a year. Each names the office this person is on the 2026 list for; Abdul Abdi's says he is running for re-election.
The Moorhead and election-archive pages also carry family, occupation and residence details. None of that is recorded here.
notes: Web search was already used up for the whole session (200 of 200) before this part began, so no search was run. Pages were read directly with the kit's own User-Agent, robots.txt obeyed: the campaign sites the candidates filed, the counties', cities' and school districts' own pages, the Minnesota DFL's endorsed list and the University of Minnesota's election archive. Campaign sites nobody filed, party-unit endorsement pages and news reports could not be looked for, so a blank here is not proof that nothing exists.

Out of reach and not worked around: cainforjudge.com (Christopher Cain's filed site) answers with a CAPTCHA page; meymanformn.com refused the connection; Wabasha County, the City of Bemidji and Three Rivers Park District ask scripts to stay out in robots.txt, as does the Hastings district's board page; the Cloquet and Marshall districts' board pages were not found at a readable address; the Faribault County Attorney page does not name the office holder.

Not on the present boards per the governments' own pages (so no office recorded): Gabe Perkins (Olmsted County lists David Senjem for the Second District), Jason Duffy (Mower District 3), Dan Delaney (Pipestone District 4), Alicia Schaupp (Lakeville council), Rachelle Hamilton (New Hope council), Amy Puschinsky (White Bear Lake board), Al Dahlgren (St. Cloud board; the district's election page shows him filing campaign finance reports in 2024, 2025 and 2026), Amy Smith (Rockford board).

Jon Koznick's own Endorsements page lists the Republican Party of Minnesota among his endorsers, but the site's dated posts are from 2020 and the page gives no year, so it is not recorded as a statement about 2026. No Republican party unit's own page was reached for him, Calvin Bahr or Charlie Kistler.

Tim Parkin's About page says he has worked for the Olmsted County Sheriff's Office since 2007 and is a Captain there today; that is employment, not an elected or appointed office, so it is not recorded under offices. Whether it should show is John's decision.

Bob Bambenek: the election archive's record (Winona County; offices held: Winona County Recorder) gives a full birth date; only the year is recorded, marked secondary. Two anchors: Winona County, Minnesota, and the Recorder's office.
Abdul Abdi: the district's Board Member Finder gives his term as 2023-2027, though the District 1 seat is on the November 2026 ballot; recorded as the page states it.
The DFL list spells Zack Meyman's first name Zach; the district (House 19B) matches.

Nothing citable was reached for Calvin Bahr and Jon Koznick (sitting legislators, whose record pages exist already), Gabe Perkins, Jason Duffy, Dan Delaney, Cory Kubista, Cameron Davis, Dan Rasmussen, Alicia Schaupp, Rachelle Hamilton, Marga Ybarra, Emelie Rivera, Annie Saboe, Kendal Larson, Sara Brink, Al Dahlgren, Amy Smith and Christopher Cain.
